chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Abd Allah ibn Sinan from Abu Basir who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man hunted a gazelle while he was in the state of Ihram, and he broke its arm or leg, so the gazelle went on its face (limping), and he did not know what to do with it. He said: Upon him is its fidyah (ransom). I said: But he saw it afterwards walking. He said: Upon him is one-quarter of its value.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah, where specific rules apply
key_terms.رُبُعُ ثَمَنِهِ: One-quarter of its value, the specific compensation ruled in this case
key_terms.ظَبِي: Gazelle, a type of wild animal hunted in Arabia
key_terms.فِدَاء: Ransom or compensation paid for breaking a ritual rule or injuring an animal

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation (fidyah) for injuring a hunted animal while in Ihram?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the proportional fidyah for injuring a gazelle while in Ihram, ruling that if the animal survives and walks, the compensation is one-quarter of its value. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of assessing damage based on the extent of functional impairment rather than a fixed penalty, distinguishing it from the full value required for death. It serves as a key precedent for calculating *dam* (blood money) in cases of partial injury to game animals during the Hajj or Umrah rituals.
